name: A Bangalore terrace

place_source.title: Wikidata: Bengaluru (Q1355), coordinate location and elevation above sea level

blurb: A garden behind a Bangalore terrace: a banyan and a neem, mango, coconut and frangipani, with jasmine and bougainvillea along the wall. Mynas, bulbuls, sunbirds and magpie-robins by day, house crows and black kites overhead, flying foxes and toads after dark, geckos on the wall.

facts.text: Bengaluru has a tropical savanna climate (Köppen Aw) with distinct wet and dry seasons.

source.title: Wikipedia: Bengaluru

facts.text: Bengaluru stands about 920 m above sea level, and its elevation gives it a more moderate climate than the surrounding plains.

source.title: Wikidata: Bengaluru (Q1355), elevation above sea level

facts.text: The monsoon brings most of Bengaluru's rainfall from June to September, with September the wettest month.

source.title: Wikipedia: Bengaluru

facts.text: The Indian flying fox is one of the largest bats in the world; a city roost can hold thousands of bats in a few tall trees.
